title: Only 8% Pass This Paramedic Entrance Exam
summary: Scene hazards, vital signs and rapid-response decisions test whether you can think clearly when every clue matters.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge contains ten entrance-style questions across anatomy, observations, numeracy, communication, safety and priority judgement. It tests careful reasoning rather than local protocols or operational procedures.

Choose the best answer using only the information shown. Safe options favour recognising risk, communicating clearly and seeking appropriate qualified support.

This is not an accredited paramedic entrance exam, clinical assessment, qualification, training course or source of emergency advice.

steps: Complete ten carefully selected questions in one focused challenge.
Choose one answer each time. Correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.
Reveal your result, skill breakdown and complete answer review after the final question.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited paramedic entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Emergency procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local guidance and appropriately qualified emergency professionals.

paramedic-r2q4.question: Which statement best describes the kidneys?

answers.a1: They exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide
answers.a2: They remove wastes from blood and help regulate water balance

paramedic-r1q4.question: A live electrical cable lies across the only doorway. What comes first?

answers.a2: Keep everyone clear and get qualified help to make it safe
answers.a3: Move it with a dry object
answers.a4: Ask a bystander to watch it

paramedic-r6q2.question: A person keeps nodding but has not understood. What should happen next?

answers.a1: Repeat the same explanation more slowly
answers.a2: Ask, ‘Do you understand?’ and continue if they say yes
answers.a3: Shorten the explanation but keep the same terminology
answers.a4: Use plain words and check back

paramedic-r5q6.context: Person A feels well and their observations remain steady. Person B is newly clammy and dizzy, and their pulse has risen across three checks.
paramedic-r5q6.question: Who needs attention first?

answers.a1: Person B, because several changes point to deterioration
answers.a2: Person A, because their observations were recorded first
answers.a3: Both can wait because neither has a named diagnosis
answers.a4: Person A, because their observations are currently stable

paramedic-r10q4.context: INCIDENT RECORD — An aggressive person is throwing objects near the entrance. Equipment partly blocks the nearest exit route.
paramedic-r10q4.question: What is the safest response to the combined hazards?

answers.a1: Keep clear, move others towards a safer route and alert appropriate help
answers.a2: Approach and argue until the person stops
answers.a3: Retrieve the equipment beside the person before leaving
answers.a4: Ask an untrained bystander to block the thrown objects
